target: route "b3-level": The third blow-up level — realise B^3 (7-cube, height 22) and measure the cost of one level

findings.defect: Stated and marked PROVED, but FALSE as written. The proof's contradiction step -- "g_j would be constant on the inner cube, impossible for a coordinate of a USO of dimension >= 2" -- is false: constant (combed) coordinates are ubiquitous in USOs. The lemma's hypotheses place no restriction on the inner dimension m, and at m = 1 (the paper's own realised first blow-up level) g_j is constant automatically, so the contradiction can never be reached there. I built an explicit instance in which conclusion (c) fails. GAP (the exact missing hypothesis, one sentence): b3:rise-sign(c) holds only under the additional hypothesis that the edge direction g_j is non-constant on the inner cube of s -- which does hold for s = B^2, j = alpha_2, so the level-three application survives, but the lemma as stated does not.
findings.evidence: COUNTEREXAMPLE (built and verified from the game, exact rationals, three independent code paths -- my own normal-form solver, my own lem:dyadic-row game builder, and the harness mycore.py). Nondegenerate stopping ONE-player SSG on 90 vertices (3 Max, 85 average, 2 sinks), denominator 2^8, harmonic normal form over targets (x, alpha_1, beta_1 | t_1) in 256ths, remaining mass to t_0:  x: (32,68,143|1) and (0,0,0|94);  alpha_1: (248,4,3|0) and (1,0,120|8);  beta_1: (0,137,98|13) and (77,17,100|0).  Verified from the game: out-degree two everywhere, greatest trap empty (mycore.is_stopping True), no tied incidence, improvement outmap = (0,1,3,6,7,4,5,2) = B^1 = B_{p,e_0}(1-cube) with p = parity and z = o xor u = e_0, AUSO, sink 0, h* = 4, walk 4,3,5,1,0. Here the translated coordinate is j = x (the inner coordinate), and w = p^{x,1} - p^{x,0} = (-1/8, -17/64, -143/256): every entry strictly NEGATIVE, so "w has entries of both signs" fails. Parts (a) and (b) do hold in this instance (all rises nonnegative; w.rise = -0.2329, -0.1845 at v = 0,1 matching Delta_x(y_v) < 0 < Delta_x(x_v)), so it is precisely (c) that is false. Falsity of the asserted step, independently: enumerating all USOs, ALL 12 USOs of the 2-cube and 680 of the 744 USOs of the 3-cube have a constant coordinate (all of them acyclic). findings.defect: The measurement does NOT reproduce. The remark's final sentence -- "At the other six, w.(I-M_v)^{-1}b_v > 0 carries the easy direction - -> +" -- is false at two of the six inner strategies it names. At v = 0 the quantity is exactly 0 (because b_0 is the zero vector: at that strategy no selected row of I u Y carries any weight on the beta_2 slot, so the whole I u Y block does not move between the layers at all), and at v = 1 it is strictly NEGATIVE. Both are strategies at which g_{beta_1} on layer (0,0) is +, so at v = 0 and v = 1 the level-two game reverses the margin in the "easy" direction with a CONSTANT Min response and with zero (resp. wrongly-signed) restricted rise -- by a mechanism the remark's formula does not capture. The remark's headline conclusion ("the Min vertex is a profile switch", the identity holding at 0,1,2,4,5,6 and failing at 3,7 exactly where the Min response changes) does reproduce; it is the sign sentence that fails.

findings.defect: The identity itself is correct and reproduces exactly, but the closing clause of the statement -- "the sign of the transfer impedance ...; by b3:rise-sign it must follow g_j" -- is FALSE, because b3:rise-sign's sign identity is for the FULL coefficient vector p^{j,1}-p^{j,0} on all of C, while b3:rise-direction restricts w to I u Y and thereby silently drops j's own weight on the beta slot (56/512 for beta_1 in prop:b2-realised). This is the same root cause as the b3:min-role failure and it is load-bearing: b3:residue's reading of the search ("the search settles on the PURE BOOST, which by b3:rise-direction can reverse in one direction only") and next_steps item (4) ("prove that no family of rows can satisfy b3:rise-sign(c) ... which by b3:rise-direction is a statement about the sign pattern of the transfer impedances w.(I-M_v)^{-1}b_v") both rest on the restricted-w statement and are therefore unsupported. GAP (one sentence): b3:rise-direction's sign conclusion follows g_j only when the row difference p^{j,1}-p^{j,0} vanishes outside I u Y, i.e. when the translated coordinate j does not itself read the new outer pair; otherwise the sign of the FULL rise (the I u Y impedance extended by 1 in the beta slot and A in the alpha slot) is what must follow g_j.

findings.defect: Rediscovery presented as new. Part (a) -- that B_{p,z}(s) is an AUSO for EVERY parity function p and EVERY z -- is already in frontier.tex and is machine-checked: rem:blowup-measured (l.5214) states that lean/SSGProof/Blowup.lean proves "isUSO_blow (for every z and every parity function)" and "isAcyclic_blow (likewise)", and the Lean source confirms both theorems are universally quantified over (z : V iota) and (par : V iota -> Bool). The route neither cites this nor flags the overlap, and the headline calls it "a 2^23-fold relaxation of the level-three target that thm:blowup did not expose". What IS genuinely new and correctly proved is (b) -- the walk length h(u)+2+h(o xor z) for arbitrary z with p agreeing with the parity only ALONG THE WALK (Lean's walk_blow fixes z = o xor u and par = parOf h globally) -- and the identification of the sink for arbitrary z (the paper says the sink identification is not formalised).

findings.defect: The proposition's structural content is correct and verified, but its closing numeric clause does not follow and is mis-rounded. (i) "lift the readout of alpha_2 by at least 0.065" is derived as Theta - 0.5538, which is 0.06435 -- less than 0.065, so the rounding overstates the bound. (ii) More seriously, 0.5538 is the cap on the PUBLISHED level-two game's own inner values, whereas in a level-three realisation the inner rows must change (they must read the new outer pair, as the same sentence says), so their values are not bounded by 0.5538 and the figure constrains nothing about a level-three realisation. (iii) The supporting sentence "Psi > Theta needs some vertex read by Psi to have value > Theta" is true only if t_1 counts as a vertex read (a row may put weight on t_1, whose value is 1); the proof's justification "|p|_1 + q <= 1 and val <= 1" is what makes it work, and should say so.

findings.defect: Two unstated hypotheses and one unjustified parenthetical. (i) The lemma writes F := f - Ah - q and H := h - A'f as functions of z_v alone and uses monotonicity of h in z; this needs f and h (the two action-1 rows) to be functions of the INNER values only, i.e. not to read alpha or beta. The stated hypothesis is only "the inner vertices do not read the outer pair", which does not give it. (ii) "if the denominator vanishes the design is infeasible" does not follow: pi.(z_* - z_{v'}) = 0 makes the displayed ratio bound vacuous (the derived inequality pi.(z_v - z_{v'}) > (1-AA')(Theta - f(z_{v'})) remains satisfiable), it does not contradict the design. WHAT BREAKS. (1) b3:rise-sign(c) is FALSE as stated -- I built and verified an explicit 90-vertex nondegenerate stopping one-player SSG realising B^1 = B_{p,e_0}(1-cube) in which w = p^{x,1}-p^{x,0} = (-1/8,-17/64,-143/256) is single-signed. Its proof's contradiction step ("no coordinate of a USO of dimension >= 2 is constant") is false: all 12 USOs of the 2-cube and 680 of the 744 of the 3-cube have a constant coordinate. Repairable by adding the hypothesis that g_j is non-constant on the inner cube, which does hold for s = B^2, j = alpha_2. (2) b3:min-role's sign measurement fails at two of the six strategies it names (exactly 0 at v = 0, strictly negative at v = 1). (3) b3:rise-direction's closing inference "by b3:rise-sign it must follow g_j" is false because the restricted w drops j's own weight on the beta slot; this is the load-bearing step for b3:residue's "the pure boost can reverse in one direction only" and for next_steps item (4), both of which are therefore unsupported.

STANDING-ERROR SWEEP: clean. val_sigma is everywhere taken as the componentwise minimum over BOTH positional tau with attainment asserted (never greedy policy iteration); rows are accumulated, never dict literals (I re-verified this on the route's build.py and used the same discipline); fresh vertices carry 'T0'/'T1' sentinels mapped to indices only at the end and every successor index is in range; the greatest trap is computed by lem:trapchar and is empty in all three games. The route claims no decision rule, barrier, lower bound, polynomial class or target-equivalent oracle, so THE STANDING RULE, the own-successor/Z_0-Z_1 requirements and the vacuous-stall test do not apply. The b3:tb witness is dyadic, was built as a game, and was verified from the game -- the round-15 "witness that is not a game" trap is not repeated. The run length 12 counts productive steps only (the terminal vertex 4 is the sink).

BOTTOM LINE. The route's central positive claim -- that a 194-vertex nondegenerate stopping SSG realises B_{p,0}(B^2), the blow-up's outer machinery at the third level, with an affinely readable surrogate parity that agrees with the true parity along the walk -- is fully correct and independently verified from the game, as are b3:free-parity(b), b3:translate, b3:b3, b3:two-cycle, b3:decompose and every numeric claim I recomputed. The honest headline ("B^3 is NOT realised") stands. What must be repaired before integration is the necessary-condition layer: b3:rise-sign(c) needs a hypothesis it does not have (and is false without it), b3:min-role's final sentence must be withdrawn, and b3:rise-direction's "must follow g_j" clause must be restated for the full coefficient vector -- after which the route's reading of its own search residue (b3:residue) and its proposed negative programme (next_steps 4) no longer follow from anything proved.
